blocks.prompt: 5. [Prove by mathematical induction:] \(n! > 2^n - 1\) for integral values of \(n \ge 4\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh inequality (ghair-barabari) hai jo \(n = 4\) se shuru hoti hai, 1 se nahi. Is liye extended induction (barhaya hua induction) lagayenge, jis ka base case \(n = 4\) hai.
\(n = 1, 2, 3\) par yeh ghalat hai: \(1 > 1\), \(2 > 3\), \(6 > 7\) teeno nahi chalte. Isi liye sawal \(n \ge 4\) kehta hai.
Plan: hypothesis ko \(k + 1\) se multiply karna, phir \(k + 1 \ge 5\) ka faida utha kar \(2^{k+1} - 1\) tak pohanchna. Inequality mein barabar wala hisaab nahi hota; humein bas dikhana hota hai ke ek cheez doosri se bari hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(S(n): n! > 2^n - 1\).
Saabit karna hai: \(S(n)\) har integer \(n \ge 4\) ke liye sahi hai.
Tareeqa: Extended mathematical induction: \(S(4)\) check karna; kisi \(k \ge 4\) par \(S(k)\) ko sahi maanna; phir \(S(k + 1)\) saabit karna.

Base case: \(n = 4\) rakhein
\[4! = 24\]
\[2^4 - 1 = 15\]
\[24 > 15\]
Is liye \(S(4)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: \(4! = 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1 = 24\) aur \(2^4 = 16\). Pehla domino yahan \(n = 4\) hai.

Induction hypothesis: \(S(k)\) ko sahi maan lein, \(k \ge 4\)
\[k! > 2^k - 1 \quad (A)\]
Kyun: Kisi integer \(k \ge 4\) par inequality ko sahi farz kiya.

Inductive step: (A) ko \(k + 1\) se multiply karein
\[(k + 1)! = (k + 1)\,k!\]
\[> (k + 1)(2^k - 1)\]
Kyun: Factorial ki tareef se \((k + 1)! = (k + 1) \times k!\). Inequality ke dono taraf positive number \(k + 1\) se multiply karne se nishan \(>\) wahi rehta hai. Yahan hypothesis istemal hui.
Dhyan dein: Negative number se multiply karte to nishan ulta ho jata; yahan \(k + 1\) positive hai, is liye fikr nahi.

\(k + 1 \ge 5\) ka faida uthayein
\[(k + 1)(2^k - 1) \ge 5(2^k - 1)\]
\[= 5 \cdot 2^k - 5\]
\[= 2^{k+1} - 1 + (3 \cdot 2^k - 4)\]
Kyun: \(k \ge 4\) hai, to \(k + 1 \ge 5\), aur \(2^k - 1\) positive hai; is liye \(k + 1\) ki jagah 5 rakhne se value chhoti ya barabar hogi. Phir \(5 \cdot 2^k\) ko \(2 \cdot 2^k + 3 \cdot 2^k = 2^{k+1} + 3 \cdot 2^k\) mein tora, aur \(-5 = -1 - 4\) likha, taake target \(2^{k+1} - 1\) alag nazar aaye.

Nateeje jorein
\[3 \cdot 2^k - 4 \ge 3 \cdot 16 - 4 = 44 > 0\]
\[(k + 1)! > 2^{k+1} - 1\]
Is liye \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hai.
Kyun: \(k \ge 4\) par \(2^k \ge 16\), is liye extra hissa \(3 \cdot 2^k - 4\) positive hai. Ek chain bani: \((k + 1)! > (k + 1)(2^k - 1) \ge 2^{k+1} - 1 + \text{(positive)} > 2^{k+1} - 1\).

Conclusion
\(S(4)\) sahi hai aur har \(k \ge 4\) ke liye \(S(k)\) se \(S(k + 1)\) sahi hota hai. Principle of extended mathematical induction se \(n! > 2^n - 1\) har integer \(n \ge 4\) ke liye sahi hai.
Kyun: Pehla domino \(n = 4\) wala gira, aur har domino agle ko girata hai, to 4 se aage sab girenge.

Tasdeeq: \(n = 5\)
\[5! = 120\]
\[2^5 - 1 = 31,\quad 120 > 31 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Inequality sahi hai, aur factorial power of 2 se bahut tezi se barhta hai, is liye farq barhta hi jata hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(n! > 2^n - 1\) har integer \(n \ge 4\) ke liye.
